newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Global telecom call rates compromise deal near - ITU.
newsitem.headline: Global telecom call rates compromise deal near - ITU.

text.p: Recommendations for a global deal to slash the cost of international telephone calls should be finalised by the end of this year, a senior International Telecommunication Union (ITU) official said on Wednesday.

Michael Calvano, the global telecommunications regulator's Southeast Asia representative, said a multi-national ITU study group would decide on recommendations for the future of so-called accounting rates by the end of December.
"It will be a decision that everybody can live with," Calvano told reporters on the sidelines of a meeting of Southeast Asian regulators.

Accounting rates are used to decide how much telephone companies pay each other for international calls. They were designed to compensate phone companies in recipient countries for the cost of completing calls.
The ITU believes the current system is obsolete and should be replaced by one based on market forces and true cost.
Prices charged for international calls in the country of call completion sometimes reach in excess of 500 percent of true costs, ITU officials estimate.
The U.S. has led calls for an agreement and unilaterally slashed 50 percent of its own international settlement rate in December.
Developing nations are worried that drastic reductions in the rates will deprive them of a vital source of revenue.
Burma, which was attending Wednesday's meeting of regional regulators, would not accept huge cuts in accounting rates, the head of the country's sole operator and regulator told Reuters.
"We have to work this thing out on our own. We are a developing country and we need the revenue," said U Htay Aung, managing director of Myanmar (Burma) Posts & Telecommunications.
"Maybe we can have these discussions at some point in the future," he said.

Delegates from other countries at the meeting -- Brunei, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam -- were more supportive of the ITU and said they hoped for a successful resolution to the issue in the near term.
"A resolution is close," said a Malaysian delegate who declined to be identified. Any discussion of the issues at the regional meeting were likely to be superceded by the ITU report, he added.
Phisal Jorphochaudom of the Communications Authority of Thailand said Bangkok was supportive of the ITU's stance on reform.
"We have the same view as the ITU. Possibly we will see a solution by the year end," he told reporters.
